people.gloss: Sit and watch the clouds rise (Vương Duy)
people.role: Abbot and founder of Vân Khởi Quán (540); the empty mountain's last student
people.appearance: A thin, very old man in patched grey hemp who walks slowly uphill and sits down wherever the path ends, as if he had been waiting there.
people.backstory: Tống Tọa Vân was a woodcutter's son from Tiều Ca Trấn, the town whose singers Không Sơn Viện had asked to sing more quietly (A033). At nine he carried wood up to the academy and stayed to sweep it. In 460 its master, Thôi Bất Kiến (thoi_bat_kien), took him as his only disciple (C094). In 488 the last abbot of Bão Nhất Quán, Cống Thủ Nhất (cong_thu_nhat), came down to the academy as a guest when his spring dried (V022), and taught him the Rule of an abbey. In 500 Thôi, who had no heir, gave the hills, his whisk and his one student to Phùng Yên Hà (phung_yen_ha) (C100). Tống went where he was given. He served Thúy Vi for forty years, and in 540 he asked to leave. He walked up the stream above the ridge until the water ended, sat down, and founded Vân Khởi Quán where he sat (C114). In 1080 the mica ran thin, and he said that clouds, too, pass (A046). He is 780 and has kept the abbey poor, quiet and open for 660 years. He walks with Ngu Lam Sơn (ngu_lam_son) and Thường Độc Hoạt (thuong_doc_hoat) on Thủy Cùng Phong. He has never held a killing art.
people.wants: To leave the abbey to someone who can sit as Thôi sat, and to die on Thủy Cùng Phong at the place where the water ends.
people.secret: Thôi taught him the first nine layers of the Empty Mountain Sutra before the gift of 500 (the last six went only to Phùng Yên Hà), and Thúy Vi does not know that he has them. Every year since 520, on the night of Thôi's death, a monk of the abbey has gone through the haze behind the sealed gate and read those nine layers aloud in the empty academy, as Tống promised Thôi: on the empty mountain no one is seen, but voices are heard. The traveller of 1195 heard Văn Nhân Hưởng (A048). Thường Độc Hoạt shows the readers the way.

people.role: The Reader: reads the Empty Mountain Sutra aloud in Không Sơn Viện once a year
people.appearance: A small, sharp-eyed woman with a mica-miner's cracked hands and a reader's voice, low and very clear, that carries through stone.
people.backstory: Văn Nhân Hưởng was born at the mica mine of Vân Mẫu Khoáng, where the vein had been running thin since 1080 (A046), and came up to the abbey at eleven because it fed anyone who could sit still. She could not sit still, but she could remember anything she heard once, and she read aloud better than anyone the abbey had. In 1180 the abbot Tống Tọa Vân (tong_toa_van) gave her the bell of the empty hall and made her the Reader. Once a year, on the night Thôi Bất Kiến died, Thường Độc Hoạt (thuong_doc_hoat) of Thúy Vi walks her up through the haze to a crack behind the gate Thúy Vi sealed in 830 (A043). She rings the bell at the door of Không Sơn Viện and reads the nine layers of the Empty Mountain Sutra that the abbot holds aloud to the empty rooms until dawn. In 1195 a traveller sleeping in the next room heard her (A048), and the cape has talked of a ghost ever since. Tống chose her because her root is Metal: the sutra runs on Earth and Wood, and the abbot meant the reading to be a promise kept, not a teaching given.
people.wants: To understand what she has been reading for twenty years, and to read it once in daylight, with Thúy Vi's leave, so that it is no longer a secret.
people.secret: She has tried to cultivate the sutra's first three layers anyway, against her root. It has scarred a meridian, and the abbot does not know. She has also written the nine layers down, which nobody outside Thúy Vi has done since Thôi.

people.role: Prior (giám viện); runs the school and the novices
people.appearance: A square grey man with a jade-cutter's forearms who teaches letters with a stick and never uses it.
people.backstory: Born on Thúy Vi's ridge into the jade-cutters' family that served the sect, the family Cù Thúy Bách (cu_thuy_bach) came from. At twelve his Wood was too thin for the gate. Cù walked him up to the abbey herself. He has been prior since 1019, when Mâu Hành Đáo (mau_hanh_dao) died in the avalanche, and he runs the school that takes the ridge's turned-away children. He thinks the yearly reading puts the abbey at Thúy Vi's mercy.
people.wants: To end the yearly reading before it puts the abbey wholly at Thúy Vi's mercy.
people.secret: For a year he has covered the abbey's missing jars of lamp oil out of his own allowance, not knowing where they go, to spare Hàn Thanh Đài (han_thanh_dai) the blame.

people.role: Keeper of the mica and the Cloud Mother Seal
people.appearance: A pale woman who holds every stone up to the light before she speaks to the person who brought it.
people.backstory: A pine-village girl from Tùng Yên Thôn who came up to the abbey in 1022 and never went down. She cut the last clear pane of mica from Vân Mẫu Khoáng in 1080, the year the abbot said clouds also pass (A046), and made it into the mirror every seal is stamped through. She counts every pane. She trades seal-work with Thúy Vi's mica-grinder Tuân Vân Mẫu (tuan_van_mau) and will not say how much clear mica is left.
people.wants: To keep the last clear mica hidden until the abbot dies.
people.secret: She is selling the small clear panes to Tuân Vân Mẫu (tuan_van_mau) for Thúy Vi silver and writing them into the ledger as spoiled.

people.role: Teaches the novices the walk; turned away by Thúy Vi's inner gate
people.appearance: A broad, quiet man who smells of lime and always has a white pebble in his hand.
people.backstory: A lime-burner's son from Thiêu Hôi Thôn, the village Quyền Thanh Lam (quyen_thanh_lam) came from, who spent thirty years in Thúy Vi's outer gate on his Earth. In 1150 Phạm Thủ Điền (pham_thu_dien) told him, kindly, that the inner gate would not open, and he walked up to the abbey the next spring. He reached Trúc Cơ there in 1176. Now he walks the novices up the hill streams each morning, and once a year leads them the five days (some 80 km) to the water's end at Thủy Cùng Phong. He writes every year to the Earth-rooted girl in Thúy Vi's outer gate, Mễ Điền Nhi (me_dien_nhi), to say the door here is open.
people.wants: To see one of his turned-away novices sit as long as the abbot's master did.
people.secret: For every novice he walks to the water's end he sets a white pebble on a cairn off the path, and the cairn now stands taller than he does.

people.backstory: Born to a Vân Gian Trấn schoolteacher in the town among the clouds, and Tống Tọa Vân's (tong_toa_van) first disciple. She wrote down the novices' walk in 830 and ran the abbey for him for three centuries. In the winter of 1019 the avalanche buried her birthplace's upper street. She came down and dug for six days beside a nineteen-year-old Thúy Vi boy, Nhạc Chính Hành (nhac_chinh_hanh), whose family was under it, and the second slide took her (V031).
